links.outcome: Referral accuracy of LLMs run silently on live CHW encounters versus CHW decisions
links.effect: Silent trial showed CHW referral accuracy 97.9% (95% CI 96.1-98.9); o3 performed similarly to CHWs, while Gemini 2.5-Flash had 47.3% (95% CI 42.6-52.1), revealing large model differences before activation.
links.quote: CHWs demonstrated high referral accuracy (97.9% [95% CI: 96.1%-98.9%]), and OpenAI’s o3 performed similarly to CHWs while Gemini 2.5-Flash showed low accuracy (47.3% [95% CI: 42.6%-52.1%]).

links.outcome: Comparison of two LLMs and CHWs on referral accuracy using the same encounters
links.effect: o3 performed similarly to CHWs (97.9%); Gemini 2.5-Flash accuracy was 47.3% (95% CI 42.6-52.1), so choice of LLM is a critical design decision.
links.quote: In conclusion, the choice of LLM appears to be a critical design decision.

links.outcome: LLM performance on Kinyarwanda spoken CHW-patient encounters
links.effect: Encounters recorded in Kinyarwanda were processed by LLMs; o3 performed similarly to CHWs (97.9%) whereas Gemini 2.5-Flash had low accuracy (47.3%).
links.quote: Across 150 participating Rwandan CHWs, 429 encounters were recorded (in Kinyarwanda) and then processed by LLMs.

links.outcome: Completeness of LLM-generated differential diagnoses and management plans
links.effect: o3 outperformed Gemini on differential diagnosis and management plan quality, though both models missed important conditions.
links.quote: Assessment of LLM-generated differential diagnoses and management plan quality showed superior performance from o3 compared with Gemini, though both models missed important conditions.

screen.reason: Evaluates LLMs processing real recorded encounters in a silent trial to assess accuracy in community health worker referral decisions.
